still.caption: The rain stopped at 2:11 AM. This appeared on the north trail minutes later.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 001 — No matching tracks were found within 40 meters.

reel.caption:
24 minutes before the tracks were found, the North Trail unit recorded this.

Whatever crossed the trail never entered the frame completely.

NORTH TRAIL // FIELD LOG 001
reel.comment:
FIELD LOG 001 — 02:11 AM

No matching return trail was found within 40 meters.

The next usable recording came from CAMERA 07.

still.caption:
It was already in the frame.

We checked the recording three times before anyone noticed it.

CAMERA 07 // 02:17:43 AM
still.comment:
FIELD LOG 002 —

The camera never triggered a second time.

Nothing left the frame.

reel.caption:
CAMERA 07 recorded this six minutes after the tracks were found.

Nothing entered the frame.

It was already there.

CAMERA 07 // FIELD LOG 002
reel.comment:
FIELD LOG 002 — 02:17 AM

No second trigger was recorded.

The next inspection found Camera 07 in a location we did not install it.

still.caption:
This boulder was not here yesterday.

The creek is unchanged. The trail is unchanged.

The stone is not.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 003 — No drag marks were found on either bank.

reel.caption:
The crossing was clear on yesterday’s survey.

By morning, this was standing in the creek.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 003 — Water flow changed around the stone. The surrounding mud did not show an approach path.

still.caption:
The forest went silent first.

The recorder kept running.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 004 — Insects and frogs stopped at the same second. The rain did not.

reel.caption:
Listen before you look.

The silence starts before anything moves.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 004 — The biological noise floor dropped almost instantly, then returned after the movement ended.

still.caption:
Both sides of the bridge failed at the same height.

Nothing below it was disturbed.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 005 — The break points were measured separately. The heights matched.

reel.caption:
The bridge did not collapse.

It was separated.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 005 — No fresh impact marks were found on the deck or ravine walls.

still.caption:
The fog moved upstream.

The water did not.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 006 — Leaves and surface debris continued downstream the entire time.

reel.caption:
Watch the water first.

Then watch the fog.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 006 — Wind markers agreed with the creek. Only the fog moved against them.

still.caption:
Camera 07 was found 28 feet above the trail.

We did not put it there.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 007 — Rangefinder reading: 28.0 FT. No climbing gear or lower mounting marks were found.

reel.caption:
We found Camera 07 again.

This time, we had to look up.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 007 — The mounting point was intact. The original ground-level mount was empty.

still.caption:
Tonight’s footage matches a file from 1998.

Same trail. Same gap between the trees.
still.comment: ARCHIVE 008 — The older recording was catalogued before Camera 07 existed.

reel.caption:
We thought the old file was unrelated.

Then we matched the frame.
reel.comment: ARCHIVE 008 — The two recordings are separated by 28 years.

still.caption:
The 1998 map shows a river where the trail is now.

No river appears on the current survey.
still.comment: ARCHIVE 009 — The old river line follows today’s trail almost exactly.

reel.caption:
The map is old.

The alignment is not approximate.
reel.comment: ARCHIVE 009 — We checked the scale twice. The mapped river and present trail overlap.

still.caption: The first rule was written after the first incident. No one recorded what happened before it.
still.comment: FIELD RULE 01 — If the forest repeats your rhythm, leave the trail. Do not answer it.

reel.caption:
FIELD RULE 01 was not written as a warning.

It was written as a procedure.
reel.comment: FIELD RULE 01 — If the forest repeats your rhythm, leave. Do not answer the second pattern.

still.caption:
You hear it before you see it.

That is the part the old reports got right.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 010 — The first branch failure came from outside the camera view.

reel.caption:
The sound came first.

The movement came later.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 010 — The second sound was closer than the first. Nothing crossed the trail.

still.caption: The marks were too high for anything we expected to find on this trail.
still.comment: The highest gouge was measured at just under twelve feet. No lower climbing marks were found.

reel.caption:
We measured every mark we could reach.

The highest one was nearly twelve feet up.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 013 — No lower claw or climbing sequence connected to the upper gouges.

still.caption:
The tree moved twice.

We only arrived after the second position was recorded.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 012 — Two separate drag paths were visible in the mud.

reel.caption:
The tree is not moving in this recording.

The ground shows that it already did.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 012 — Both drag grooves end at the same root cavity.

still.caption:
Camera 07 came back online from above us.

No one was in the canopy.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 015 — Signal returned before the recovery team located the camera.

reel.caption:
We were looking for Camera 07 on the trail.

It was already recording us from above.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 015 — The feed angle could not have come from the original mount.

still.caption:
The station was abandoned in 2014.

The radio answered tonight.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 016 — Power to the old receiver had been disconnected before the team arrived.

reel.caption:
The radio had been dead for twelve years.

Then it answered the check-in.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 016 — The reply was too damaged to identify a speaker. The receive light activated once.

still.caption:
It looked small until it stood up.

The trees did not move with it.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 014 — Scale was estimated from the trail marker and recovery pack in the foreground.

reel.caption:
At first, we thought it was part of the tree line.

Then its height changed.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 014 — No clear anatomy was visible at any point in the recording.

still.caption:
Only one set going in.

Nothing came back out.
still.comment: FIELD ARCHIVE 018 — The note was recovered with the original trail photograph.

reel.caption:
The note was short enough to miss.

The photograph made it worse.
reel.comment: FIELD ARCHIVE 018 — No second outbound track set was documented in the recovered file.

still.caption:
Only one camera saw it.

Both cameras were pointed at the same trail.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 019 — The timestamps overlap. The second feed remains empty.

reel.caption:
Same trail. Same moment.

Only one recording contains the extra shape.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 019 — Frame comparison confirmed the camera positions were synchronized.

still.caption: The bark was wet. The air was cold. The exposed wood was still warm.
still.comment: Ambient temperature at the site was much lower. The exposed wood held the heat for several minutes.

reel.caption:
The rain cooled everything around it.

The exposed wood stayed warm.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 020 — The thermal difference persisted after repeated measurements.

still.caption:
Every camera skipped the same 17 minutes.

None of them lost power.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 017 — Missing interval: 02:03:00 → 02:20:00 on every active unit.

reel.caption:
The cameras did not fail one by one.

They all lost the same seventeen minutes.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 017 — No reboot or battery event was recorded during the gap.

still.caption:
CASE 001 — The Hollow Trail.

The path continues farther than the survey map allows.
still.comment: CASE 001 — No light source was visible beyond the root opening.

reel.caption:
The trail should end here.

It does not.
reel.comment: CASE 001 — Team entry was stopped before the root passage narrowed.

still.caption:
The missing pack was found twenty feet above the ground.

The straps were still closed.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 023 — No rope, climbing marks or broken lower branches were found below it.

reel.caption:
We found the pack.

Finding it did not explain how it got there.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 023 — The branch carrying the pack showed no fresh break damage.

still.caption:
The clearing had two people.

The reflection had three.
still.comment: FIELD LOG 024 — The additional figure never appears above the waterline.

reel.caption:
Count the people before you look at the water.

Then count again.
reel.comment: FIELD LOG 024 — The extra reflected figure remains through multiple ripples.

still.caption: FIELD RULE 02 — If a camera loses the trail, check above eye level.
still.comment: FIELD RULE 02 — Do not stand directly beneath the last known camera position.

reel.caption: FIELD RULE 02 exists because looking forward was not enough.
reel.comment: FIELD RULE 02 — Check above eye level before entering the blind section of trail.

still.caption:
Every camera was facing the same empty point.

No one remembers turning them.
still.comment: NETWORK LOG 026 — All active units reported normal orientation data before the clearing check.

reel.caption:
Camera 07 was not the only one recording.

By dawn, every unit was aimed inward.
reel.comment: NETWORK LOG 026 — The center of the clearing remained empty in every recovered frame.
